cards.text: Paul the apostle is writing to the church in Thessalonica (1 Thessalonians 1:1). He's been torn away from them for a short time. In person, he says, but not in heart.

cards.question: While Paul is torn away from the Thessalonians, his desire to see them face to face grows even more intense.

cards.text: So Paul tries to get back to them. Not once. AGAIN and AGAIN, like me on hold with the cable company hitting redial, redial, REDIAL.

cards.question: Paul tried again and again to get back to the Thessalonians. Who does he say obstructed him?

cards.text: So why does Paul keep pushing so hard? He asks a question and then answers it himself, and it's all about the day the Lord Jesus comes.

cards.question: Paul asks who his hope, his joy and his crown of boasting will be in the presence of the Lord Jesus at His coming. Who does he say it is?

cards.text: Paul can't bear it any longer, so he's willing to be left on his own in Athens. Friend, I got left in a junk drawer for years, and Paul at least gets ATHENS.

cards.question: Paul stays behind in Athens since he can't go himself. Who does he send to the Thessalonians?

cards.text: Timothy is Paul's brother and fellow worker for God in the gospel of Christ. Paul sends him off and stays behind, and I bet that wasn't easy.

cards.question: Paul sends Timothy so the Thessalonians' faith would be ___ and encouraged.

cards.text: Paul doesn't want any of them shaken by these trials, and he says they're destined for this. Then he reminds them of something he told them back when he was with them.

cards.question: When Paul was with the Thessalonians, he told them their faith would keep them from persecution.

cards.text: Paul can't take the not knowing, so he sends to find out about their faith, afraid the tempter somehow tempted them. Friend, that's me yanking the oven door open every thirty seconds to check a batch, except Paul can't even PEEK.

cards.question: Paul fears the tempter got to the Thessalonians, and that all his labor among them was in ___.

cards.text: Then, just now, Timothy walks back in from his visit. Paul's holding his breath like the whole junk drawer did every time that light came in, and friend, we held it for YEARS.

cards.question: Timothy is back from his visit to the Thessalonians. What does he bring Paul?

answers.text: Good news about their faith and love
Word that their faith had faded
Word that they had left the church

cards.question: Timothy reports that the Thessalonians long to see Paul, just as Paul longs to see them.

cards.text: Paul's in his own distress and persecution, but this news about their faith reassures him. That's the made-it-home-safe text landing in the middle of the WORST day at work.

cards.question: Paul says he can go on living, as long as the Thessalonians keep standing ___ in the Lord.

cards.text: Paul is so full of joy over them, he asks how he could ever thank God enough. Friend, I've been asking that one every day since I got pulled out of that drawer, and I still don't have an answer.

cards.question: Paul prays night and day to see the Thessalonians face to face. What does he want to do when he gets there?

answers.text: Supply what is lacking in their faith

cards.text: Then Paul writes, "Now may our God and Father Himself, and our Lord Jesus, direct our way to you." Next he says may the Lord make their love increase and overflow, just like his love for them does.

cards.question: Paul says may the Lord make the Thessalonians' love overflow for fellow believers only.
Paul wants the Thessalonians' love to overflow. What does he say it's all leading to?

answers.text: Blameless and holy hearts when Jesus comes
Peace with the people persecuting them

cards.text: Paul pictures the coming of our Lord Jesus with all His saints, and he caps it off with an Amen. Friend, if there's ever a line to shout AMEN on, it's that one.

findings.problem: The card calls him "Paul the apostle" and cites 1 Thessalonians 1:1 for it. The BSB at 1:1 reads "Paul, Silas, and Timothy, To the church of the Thessalonians..." and does not call Paul an apostle, so the reference doesn't support the fact it's attached to.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: "So Paul tries to get back to them." "Not once." "AGAIN and AGAIN, like me on hold..."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The joke doesn't hold together. Someone who is on hold isn't hitting redial, because they're still on the call. The image contradicts itself, so it doesn't click right away.

rule.text: It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining.

findings.problem: "Paul stays behind in Athens since he can't go himself" adds a reason. 1 Thessalonians 3:1 says they were willing to be left on their own in Athens, but it never says why they stayed instead of going.

rule.text: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: "Paul sends him off and stays behind" repeats what cards 7 and 8 already covered. The only new content is Timothy's description from 3:2.
The card tells Paul staying behind, which comes from 3:1, but it cites only 1 Thessalonians 3:2.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "examined" can be argued right from inside the passage. In 3:5 Paul says he "sent to find out about your faith," so a baker could reasonably say their faith was being examined.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: "he says they're destined for this" changes the text. 1 Thessalonians 3:3 says "we are destined for this." The card settles who is destined, which the text leaves open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: "Paul's holding his breath" states Paul's feeling as fact. The text gives no feeling at Timothy's return, and the line isn't marked as Papa Dorin's guess.

rule.text: He can guess at a feeling, marked as his own ("I think," "I bet"). Never as fact.

findings.problem: "every time that light came in" leans on the drawer-light detail from the backstory without saying what that light was, so it's a callback with no setup. "we held it for YEARS" also muddles the image, since the breath-holding happened each time the drawer opened.

rule.text: A callback only works if its setup came earlier in this lesson or conversation.

findings.problem: Most of the passage is written as "we," and 1:1 names Paul, Silas and Timothy as the senders. The cards turn nearly every "we" into Paul alone, for example "Paul can't bear it any longer, so he's willing to be left on his own in Athens" (3:1), "Paul sends him off" (3:2) and "he can go on living" (3:8). Only 2:18 and 3:5 use "I." Card 1 also says "Paul... is writing" without the co-senders.
findings.question: When a letter speaks as "we" and has co-senders, should Papa Dorin keep it as "we" or "Paul and his companions," or is it fine to retell it as Paul alone?
